Principle 17: The History of Korea
The Foundation of Korea
This is the story about how the nation of Korea was founded.
Our country’s history started about 5,000 years ago.
Once upon a time, the King of Heaven, Hwan-in, sent his son, Hwan-ung, to Earth.
While living on Earth, he married Ung-nyo who had changed from a bear into a woman.
She gave birth to a son and named him Dan-goon.
He became the founder of Korea.
The country’s ancient name was Gojoson.
The Kingdoms are Divided
After Gojoson fell, the Korean Peninsula was divided into three kingdoms: Goguryo, Baekje, and Shilla.
Later these three kingdoms united as a single nation and referred to it as the Shilla Kingdom.
The Shilla Kingdom was the most powerful in the middle of the 8th century.
It was called the Golden Age of Korean history.
The Independence of Korea and the Korean War
After Shilla fell, many other countries tried to gain power over Korea.
For a while, Korea was ruled by Japan.
Many Koreans did not like being under the power of Japan, so they fought against Japanese rule.
In 1945, Korea was liberated from Japan.
A civil war broke out in 1950 when armies from the North invaded the South.
As a result, the Korean peninsula became divided into North and South Korea.
Post-War Development of Korea
Since the end of the war in 1953, the country began to develop very quickly, especially during the 1970’s.
From then until now, the country has continued to grow rapidly.
In 1988, Korea hosted the Summer Olympic Games and in 2002, the World Cup was held in Korea, too.
I am very proud of my country and what it has accomplished during its long history.
